title: A binary search tree map
description:
Write a generic map backed by an (unbalanced) binary search tree:

```java
class TreeMapLite<K extends Comparable<K>, V> {
    void put(K key, V value)           // adds, or replaces the value of an existing key
    V get(K key)                       // null when absent
    boolean containsKey(K key)
    boolean remove(K key)              // false when absent; handles nodes with 0, 1 and 2 children
    int size()
    int height()                       // -1 for an empty tree, 0 for a single node
    List<K> keys()                     // in sorted order
    K floorKey(K key)                  // the greatest key <= key, or null
    int countBetween(K lo, K hi)       // keys with lo <= key <= hi, without visiting subtrees that cannot contain any
}
```

`null` keys throw `NullPointerException`.
hints: Write the recursive helpers so they return the (possibly new) subtree: `root = put(root, key, value)` then needs no special case for an empty tree.
For `countBetween`, a node smaller than `lo` can only have matches in its right subtree, and one larger than `hi` only in its left; skip the other side.
rules: Build the tree yourself instead of using TreeMap.

rules.message: Build the tree yourself instead of using TreeMap.
